Open Reading Frames of Transcripts from Their Sequences

Source: R/orfs.R
transcript_orfs.Rd

Computes, for every assayed transcript (every transcript of the annotation when self is a path), an open reading frame (ORF) and the sequence-level features that decide whether it is productive. Requires transcript sequences in the annotation directory (see extract_transcript_sequences()). The ORF of each transcript comes from the first applicable source (orf_source):

  1. "annotation": a complete annotated CDS. Its stop codon is added when the annotation excludes it (as GENCODE does) and the ORF is re-read from the annotated start codon to the first in-frame stop, so a CDS that does not match the sequence is corrected (annotation_cds_agrees = FALSE). Transcripts tagged seleno, ribosomal_slippage or non_ATG_start keep the annotated CDS.

  2. "projected": the start codon of the gene's canonical isoform lies in an exon of the transcript and reads ATG there; translation proceeds from that position to the first in-frame stop (the ORFanage approach). This is what rescues novel isoforms without CDS.

  3. "annotation_partial": an annotated CDS flagged incomplete (cds_start_NF / cds_end_NF) whose start could not be projected; the annotated span is kept, and when its 3' end is known the NMD rule still applies (GENCODE annotates many NMD transcripts this way).

  4. "longest": none of the above; the longest ATG-to-stop ORF of at least min_orf_length nt is used and coding_probability tells whether it is believable.

  5. "none": no ORF of at least min_orf_length nt.

From the ORF the function derives the stop codon (NA when translation runs into the transcript end, a non-stop decay substrate), the UTR lengths, uORFs in the 5' UTR (n_uorf, complete upstream ORFs; n_overlapping_uorf, out-of-frame upstream ORFs overlapping the main start), the genomic coordinates of start and stop, whether start and stop are shared with the canonical isoform and whether the reading frame at the stop codon is in frame with the canonical ORF (frame_vs_canonical), and the NMD class:

  • "ptc": the stop lies more than nmd_rule nt upstream of the last exon-exon junction (the 50-nt rule), NMD predicted.

  • "ptc_start_proximal": same, but the ORF is shorter than start_proximal nt; still called unproductive, with the note that such transcripts can escape NMD by translation re-initiation.

  • "non_stop": no in-frame stop codon.

  • "long_3utr": no premature stop, but a 3' UTR longer than long_utr3 nt (default Inf, so the flag is off unless asked for).

  • "none": no NMD feature.

  • NA: no stop codon in a transcript whose 3' end is annotated as incomplete (cds_end_NF / mRNA_end_NF, column end_incomplete), so nothing can be said.

coding_potential() scores every transcript's longest ORF with the Fickett TESTCODE statistic and an in-frame hexamer usage score, combined with the ORF length and the fraction of the transcript the ORF covers by a logistic model trained on GENCODE 50 human coding versus lncRNA transcripts (see data-raw/build_coding_model.R and build_coding_model()); coding_probability above coding_cutoff (0.364, the CPAT human cutoff) is called coding.

Usage

transcript_orfs(
  self,
  gene_name = NULL,
  min_orf_length = 90L,
  nmd_rule = 50,
  start_proximal = 150,
  long_utr3 = Inf,
  ...
)

coding_potential(
  self,
  gene_name = NULL,
  min_orf_length = 90L,
  coding_cutoff = 0.364,
  ...
)

Arguments

self

An IsoformicExperiment or an annotation directory path.

gene_name

Optional genes (names or IDs) to restrict the result to.

min_orf_length

Minimum ORF length in nt, stop codon included (default 90, i.e. 29 amino acids).

nmd_rule

Distance (nt) from the stop codon to the last junction above which NMD is predicted; default 50.

start_proximal

ORF length (nt) below which a premature stop is classed ptc_start_proximal instead of ptc; default 150.

long_utr3

3' UTR length (nt) above which long_3utr is flagged; default Inf.

...

Not used; reserved for methods.

coding_cutoff

Coding probability above which a transcript is called coding (default 0.364).

Value

transcript_orfs() returns a tibble with one row per transcript: transcript_id, transcript_name, gene_id, gene_name, has_sequence, orf_source, annotation_cds_agrees, orf_tx_start and orf_tx_end (ORF span in transcript coordinates, stop codon included), orf_length, protein_length, start_codon, stop_codon, orf_genomic_start, orf_genomic_end, utr5_length, utr3_length, stop_to_last_junction, nmd_class, end_incomplete, n_uorf, n_overlapping_uorf, canonical_transcript_id, start_same_as_canonical, stop_same_as_canonical, frame_vs_canonical ("in_frame", "frameshift" or "novel_sequence" when the stop lies outside the canonical isoform), and the coding potential columns longest_orf_length, orf_coverage, fickett_score, hexamer_score and coding_probability. coding_potential() returns transcript_id, transcript_name, gene_id, gene_name, the five coding potential columns and is_coding.

Stored ORF table

The analysis takes minutes for a whole GENCODE release, so the rows computed are written to annot_data_orfs.parquet in the annotation directory and read back by later calls, sessions and objects that use the same annotation. A stored row is used when the canonical isoform of the gene, among the transcripts of the call, is the one it was computed with, so the result is the same with and without the table. A gene with a transcript that has no such row is computed whole, and its rows are stored when its canonical isoform is the one of the whole annotation. The table is computed again when the transcripts, exons or sequences of the annotation, min_orf_length, the coding potential model (build_coding_model()) or the package version change. It is not written into a read-only directory or the example annotation of the installed package, and options(isoformic.orf_cache = FALSE) turns it off. The warning about sequences that differ in length from their exons is given when the rows are computed, not when they are read back.

See also

transcript_productivity(), transcript_features()

Examples

iso <- example_isoformic()
orfs <- transcript_orfs(iso, gene_name = "RBPJ")
orfs[, c("transcript_name", "orf_source", "orf_length", "nmd_class", "coding_probability")]
#> # A tibble: 65 × 5
